text:
Justin Faulk is 34, in his first season in Detroit, and playing more than 20 minutes a night on a team that needs defensemen who can handle them. His best night was Nov 2 against Florida: a power-play goal and an assist in a 5-3 win.

He's been fine. The Red Wings have 56% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and they've scored 4.7 fewer goals than those chances deserve, which has cost him points. His own three goals came on 1.0 expected, so the goals are lucky and the assists aren't.

The broader picture is a Detroit team at 7-8-3 that can't finish, playing without Dylan Larkin while he refuses to play until he's traded. Faulk is past 1,050 career games, and Evolving-Hockey had him near the middle of the league's defensemen last season with weak offensive impact (bottom 4%). His ice time is up almost two minutes over the last ten games. Our projection: about 41 points.
